texts.value: Histone H1 protein binds to linker DNA between nucleosomes forming the macromolecular structure known as the chromatin fiber (PubMed:35581345, PubMed:40240600). Histones H1 are necessary for the condensation of nucleosome chains into higher-order structured fibers and promote formation of the H3K27me3 mark by the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex (PubMed:35581345, PubMed:40240600, PubMed:40516528). Ability to associate with nucleosomes and compact chromatin depends on linker DNA length and trajectory (PubMed:35581345). Also acts as a regulator of individual gene transcription through chromatin remodeling, nucleosome spacing and DNA methylation (PubMed:40240600)
Associates with nucleosomes, promoting condensation into higher-order structured chromatin
Mainly localizes in heterochromatin (PubMed:40240600). Distributed throughout the nucleus; displays a punctuate staining pattern in the nucleus (PubMed:38530350, PubMed:40240600)
Expression is activated by transcription factor CRAMP1, in collaboration with NPAT and GON4L
The C-terminal domain is required for high-affinity binding to chromatin
Deamidation of Asn-76 and Asn-77 by CTPS1 in response to DNA damage promotes subsequent acetylation of histone H1 at Lys-75 (H1K75ac)

Acetylated at Lys-26 (PubMed:15469825). Deacetylated at Lys-26 by SIRT1 (PubMed:15469825). Acetylated at Lys-34 (H1.3K34ac) by KAT2A; H1.3K34ac is enriched at promoters of active genes and stimulates transcription by increasing H1 mobility and recruiting TAF1 (PubMed:22465951). Acetylated at Lys-75 (H1K75ac) by EP300 following deamidation of Asn-76 and Asn-77 by CTPS1 in response to DNA damage, thereby increasing chromatin accessibility to facilitate the recruitment of DNA repair proteins (PubMed:40240600)

Mono- and dimethylated at Lys-26 by EHMT2/G9a (H1.4K26me1 and H1.4K26me2, respectively) (PubMed:19144645). H1.4K26me1, H1.4K26me2 and H1.4K26me3 are demethylated by KDM4A (PubMed:19144645, PubMed:30156264). H1.4K26me is recognized by histone reader HP1 (CBX1, CBX3 and/or CBX5) (PubMed:16127177)

H1 histones are progressively phosphorylated during the cell cycle, becoming maximally phosphorylated during late G2 phase and M phase, and being dephosphorylated sharply thereafter (By similarity). Phosphorylated at Ser-27 by AURKB during mitosis (PubMed:21511733). Simultaneous methylation at Lys-26 (H1.4K26me) and phosphorylation at Ser-27 (H1.4S27Ph) prevents binding by histone reader HP1 (CBX1, CBX3 and/or CBX5) (PubMed:16127177). Phosphorylation at Ser-36 by PKA during mitosis promotes dissociation from mitotic chromosome (PubMed:21852232). Phosphorylation at Ser-187 by CDK9 is associated with transcription activation (PubMed:28539972, PubMed:33238524). Phosphorylation at Thr-146 highly increases during mitosis compared to interphase (PubMed:38530350)

Citrullination at Arg-54 (H1R54ci) by PADI4 takes place within the DNA-binding site of H1 and results in its displacement from chromatin and global chromatin decondensation, thereby promoting pluripotency and stem cell maintenance
ADP-ribosylated on Ser-150 in response to DNA damage
